method: Compared static full-config generation (stall mode, variant=none -- no movement issued at all) against movement-enabled generation (promote/demote mode's generated_control, which runs AFTER a real byte copy + round-trip verification has already been performed on the target layer's scratch region), same model/ctx/kv_type/split/prompt in both cases.

no_corruption_no_stale_reads.interpretation: poison_had_no_effect_on_output == true in every trial is EXPECTED and CORRECT given classification B (live decode never reads the scratch copy) -- it is direct proof there is no stale-read/corruption risk from this specific mechanism, precisely because the mechanism does not yet wire into the live graph. This is not the same claim as 'live tiering preserves correctness' -- there is no live tiering here to test yet (see ownership_model.json).

logit_equality: Not measured directly (only argmax token identity, via greedy decoding) -- token identity under greedy decoding is a stricter and sufficient proxy for logit equality at the tested precision (any logit divergence large enough to matter would have flipped at least one of the 8-32 argmax picks across every trial; none did).
verdict: correctness preserved in every trial -- expected outcome given classification B, not evidence of correct live tiering (none implemented yet)
